title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
authors: Y. Bai, S. Kadavath, S. Kundu, et al.
before: Harmlessness came from humans labelling large volumes of unpleasant model output.
problem: That labour is expensive, distressing, and its criteria live in labellers' heads rather than on paper.
breakthrough: Write the principles down, have the model critique and revise its own outputs against them, and train on its own feedback.
why: It moved part of alignment from tacit labelling to explicit written rules, and made the criteria auditable.
next: RLAIF more broadly, and the alignment approach behind Claude.
inherits: AI feedback against stated principles as a supplement to human preference data.
